Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

# Summary of 2001 Political Manifesto

This manifesto presents a comprehensive policy platform organised around key life stages and national priorities, centred on the theme of individual freedom, reduced government interference, and strengthened local institutions.

## Family and Education

The document proposes tax reductions for families with young children, including an increased Children's Tax Credit and a new allowance for married couples with children under eleven. The education policy advocates for "Free Schools" where headteachers and governors would have complete responsibility for running their institutions. Parents would gain the right to call for special inspections of failing schools, and successful schools would be permitted to expand. The document proposes abolishing regulations that make excluding disruptive pupils difficult, establishing separate Progress Centres for such students. Student loan repayment thresholds would be raised, and university endowment funds would be created.

## Law and Order

The manifesto commits to increasing police numbers and reducing bureaucracy. Proposals include expanding Secure Training Centres tenfold for persistent young offenders, mandatory sentences for drug dealers selling to minors, and "honesty in sentencing" where served sentences match those handed down by courts. Victims would receive named police contacts and written reasons when charges are dropped.

## Economy and Taxation

The economic platform promises £8 billion in tax cuts, including abolishing taxes on savings and dividends, reducing petrol tax by 6p per litre, and raising personal allowances for pensioners. A Deregulation Commission would scrutinise new regulations and set declining regulatory budgets for government departments. The document emphasises retaining the pound rather than joining the euro, enhanced Bank of England independence, and transparent national accounts.

## Healthcare

Healthcare policy would abolish waiting list initiatives in favour of a "Patient's Guarantee" with maximum waiting times based on clinical need. Patients unable to be treated within specified timeframes could choose private hospital treatment funded by the health authority. The document proposes removing political interference from hospital management, restoring authority to Ward Sisters, and reintroducing the Matron role. Tax penalties on private medical insurance would be abolished.

## Pensions and Elderly Care

Pensioner policy includes raising the age tax allowance by £2,000, removing one million pensioners from income tax, and increasing the basic state pension—with larger increases for over-75s. The document proposes abolishing compulsory annuity purchase at age seventy-five and consulting on funded pension alternatives for younger workers.

## Foreign Policy and Europe

The European policy advocates for a "network Europe" of nations cooperating flexibly rather than integration into a superstate. The document opposes ratifying the Nice Treaty, supports national vetoes, and commits to keeping the pound. It opposes European military structures outside NATO and supports ballistic missile defence. Asylum policy proposes housing all applicants in secure reception centres until cases are determined.

## Welfare Reform

Welfare proposals include replacing existing unemployment programmes with "Britain Works," paying independent contractors for successful long-term job placements. A "Can Work, Must Work" guarantee would require capable unemployed individuals to work or lose benefits. Anti-fraud measures include a national task force and cleanup of excess National Insurance numbers.

## Local Government and Rural Affairs

The manifesto proposes abolishing Regional Development Agencies and planned Regional Assemblies, returning powers to county councils. Planning policy would abolish national housebuilding targets and establish "Blue Belt" protections for waterways. Rural policies include cutting business rates for village shops and post offices, and implementing a recovery strategy from the foot-and-mouth crisis.

## Constitutional Reform

Constitutional proposals include allowing only English and Welsh MPs to vote on laws affecting only those nations, strengthening House of Lords independence through an independent appointments commission, requiring twice-weekly Prime Minister appearances before the Commons, and reducing the number of MPs and political advisers.
